newsitem.title: CHINA: Washington mayor Barry to visit Beijing.
newsitem.headline: Washington mayor Barry to visit Beijing.

text.p: Washington D.C. Mayor Marion Barry may preside over a virtually bankrupt city but he still has high-level friends in Beijing.
Barry is scheduled to visit the Chinese capital November 15-20 at the invitation of Beijing's acting mayor Jia Qinglin, an official of the Beijing city government said by telephone on Tuesday.
Barry and Jia would meet to "further promote bilateral friendly cooperative relations", the Xinhua news agency said.
Jia became acting mayor last month, replacing Li Qiyan in a long-delayed reshuffle after the downfall of Li's disgraced mentor, Chen Xitong.
Chen resigned as Beijing's Communist Party boss in April 1995 after one of his vice-mayors came under investigation for economic crimes and committed suicide.
Barry, a liberal Democrat and civil rights leader, is one of America's more controversial black politicians.

He has made no secret of his problems with alcohol and he served a jail term in 1990 on a federal drug charge. His arrest, trial and conviction sidelined his political career, but by 1994 he was re-elected to a fourth term as mayor.
The financial management of the District of Columbia was taken over in February last year by a federal control board.
